source_text: Mira tunc ibi cerneres et exquisita conpendia saeuiendi. Namque cum manum carnificis gladiumque ipsum tot ceruicibus deditum numerosus iustorum populus urgueret, artifex feritas dispositas agminum series per ordinem dirigebat, scilicet ut sacrilegi percussoris ictus uelut impetu quodam furoris pia colla percuteret. Deinde ut ne inexplicabile fieret cruentum illud et barbarum ministerium, hanc sibi expeditionem sceleris inuenit. Nam si uno in loco percussurus ipse consisteret, inmensam stragem corporum cumulus aceruaret; ipse denique spatium tanta strage conpletus alueus denegaret. Tunc oculis sub ictu ferri de more uelatis, nullae tamen aciem liberae mentis clausere tenebrae, sed largus atque inaestimabilis splendor inmensae lucis effulsit. Nam et plerique cum proximis et assistentibus sibi fratribus, quamuis carnaliter in uisum acies non pateret, uidere se tamen mira quaedam loquebantur, quod sibi apparerent equi desuper niueo colore candentes, quibus ueherentur iuuenes candidati. Nec defuere ex eodem martyrum numero qui collegarum relationem adtestarentur auribus et ex audito equorum fremitu ac sono recognoscerent. Ibi tunc et Marianus, prophetico spiritu iam repletus, fidenter ac fortiter praedicabat proximam iusti sanguinis ultionem, uariasque saeculi plagas uelut de caeli iam culmine minabatur, luem, captiuitates, famem, terraeque motus et cynomiae uenena cruciantia. Qua praedicatione non tantum gentilibus insultabat fides martyris, sed etiam fratribus incentiuum aemulandae uirtutis et quasi classicum praecanebat, ut inter tantas saeculi plagas a iustis dei tam bonae atque pretiosae mortis raperetur occasio.
thought_title: The mass beheading and the signs seen at death
orientation: The narrator describes the beheading of Marian, James and the other clergy together by a river outside the city.
pass_a_gloss: You would have seen wonderful things then there and carefully devised shortcuts of raging. For when the numerous people of the righteous pressed upon the hand of the executioner and the very sword given over to so many necks, skillful cruelty kept directing the drawn up rows of the columns in order, namely in order that the blow of the sacrilegious striker might strike their devoted necks as if with a certain rush of fury. Next, in order that that bloody and barbarous service might not become unmanageable, it found for itself this quick method of crime. For if he himself, about to strike, were to stand still in one place, a piled heap would heap up the immense wreck of bodies; finally the channel itself, filled up with so great wreck, would deny space. Then, with eyes veiled in the usual manner under the blow of the iron, nevertheless no darkness closed the gaze of the free mind, but a generous and immeasurable brightness of immense light shone forth. For also very many, with the brothers nearest and standing beside them, although in fleshly manner the gaze did not lie open to sight, nevertheless kept saying that they themselves saw certain wonderful things, that horses gleaming with snowy white color appeared to them from above, on which young men clothed in white were being carried. Nor were there lacking from the same number of martyrs men who would attest with their ears the report of their companions and would recognize it from the heard neighing of horses and sound. There then also Marian, already filled with prophetic spirit, was proclaiming with confidence and courage the near avenging of righteous blood, and was threatening as if already from the summit of heaven the varied blows of the world, plague, captivities, famine, and shakings of earth and tormenting poisons of the fly swarm. By this proclamation the faith of the martyr not only was taunting the pagans, but also was sounding beforehand for the brothers an incitement to imitate courage and as it were a trumpet call, in order that amid so many blows of the world the opportunity of so good and precious a death might be seized by the righteous of God.

lemmas.gloss: shortcuts, saving devices here for killing

choices.why: conpendia is a speedy way; exquisita stresses deliberate contrivance, not moral refinement
artifex makes cruelty the skilled manager arranging rows for throughput
keeps the narrator judgment that striking holy necks is sacrilege, not a neutral executioner

choices.english: tormenting poisons of the fly swarm
choices.why: cynomyia is the dog fly plague, listed among physical plagues with pestilence and famine

choices.english: as it were a trumpet call
choices.why: classicum is the military trumpet rally, fitting the call to seize death amid world blows

pass_b_english: What you would have seen there was strange, with carefully devised shortcuts for raging. A great crowd of the righteous pressed hard upon the executioner's hand and upon the very sword given over to so many necks, so skillful cruelty marched the drawn-up ranks of the column through in order, so that the blow of the sacrilegious striker would fall on holy necks with a kind of rush of fury. Lest that bloody and barbarous work become unmanageable, it found for itself this swift way of getting the crime done. If the striker himself had stood in one place to strike, the heaped pile would have heaped up an immense slaughter of bodies; in the end the riverbed itself, filled with so great a slaughter, would have allowed no room.

Then their eyes were veiled in the usual way for the blow of the iron, yet no darkness closed the gaze of their free minds, but a lavish and measureless splendor of immense light burst forth. Many spoke with the brothers next to them and standing beside them of the wonderful things they still saw, though their eyes were not bodily open to sight: horses gleaming snow-white from above, carrying young men clothed in white. Nor were martyrs lacking from that same company who confirmed their companions' report by what their ears told them, for they recognized the neighing and pounding of the horses when they heard it.

There too Marian, already filled with a prophetic spirit, proclaimed with confidence and courage the coming vengeance for righteous blood, and threatened the varied blows of the world as if already from the height of heaven: pestilence, captivities, famine, earthquakes, and the tormenting poisons of the fly swarm. By that proclamation the martyr's faith not only struck at the pagans but also sounded to the brothers an incentive to match his courage, as it were a trumpet call, so that amid so many blows of the world God's righteous would seize the chance of so good and precious a death.

last_rejected.quote: so skillful cruelty marched the drawn-up ranks of the column through in order
last_rejected.source_quote: Namque cum manum carnificis gladiumque ipsum tot ceruicibus deditum numerosus iustorum populus urgueret, artifex feritas
last_rejected.why: Namque cum is causal: because the crowd pressed on, cruelty ordered the ranks. English 'so' reads as a result or degree clause, which muddles the logic and leaves the sentence hard to follow.
last_rejected.fix: For the great crowd of the righteous pressed hard upon the executioner's hand and the sword, and so skillful cruelty marched the ranks through in order,
last_rejected.ruling: cum urgueret gives cause for dirigebat; 'so' means therefore, same logic
